title: schema.Fetcher cache never expires, so old schemas outlive a release
description: strspc-manager src/schema/schema.go: Fetch returns the file under os.UserCacheDir()/strspc/schemas whenever it exists; readCache checks only type and size, with no TTL or revalidation. After a schema release any machine with a cached entity/v1.json keeps failing RL002 on the new fields until the file is deleted. Reproduced 2026-10-30: on the real cache lint fails on inherits/overrides, with HOME pointing at an empty dir the same realm passes. Fix: add a TTL or conditional GET, keeping the stale copy as the offline fallback. Workaround: delete ~/Library/Caches/strspc/schemas (macOS).
notes:
Correction on the repro: the failing lint read the old cached entity/v1.json. That file was then rewritten at 09:58:05 by something other than the lint run, so lint passes on the real cache now. The defect stands from the code: readCache has no expiry, only replacing the file clears it.
The rewrite is explained: a parallel session deleted the stale entity/v1.json by hand during the 1.11.0 release, and its next validate refetched the file. Duplicate strspc-rules-cvk closed in favour of this bead.

title: strspc-manager: schema cache never expires, so published schema changes do not reach machines with a cached copy

After v1.11.0 reached steerspec.dev, strspc lint and realm validate still failed RL002 on an entity using inherits and overrides, because the cache held the copy from 2026-10-28; an isolated cache passed. title: pin-consumers.yml does not sync rules/_schema/ to consumers
description: pin-consumers.yml updates only the matrix files (rules/realm.json, .strspc/config.yaml and docs), never rules/_schema/. For 1.11.0 each consumer needed a hand-made sync PR (manager #156, CLI #152, sync #119, spec #18). strspc-manager v1.27.0 adds RM015, which compares a realm's _schema with its pinned core when a DependencyFetcher is supplied. Once the CLI wires that in, each core pin PR will likely fail the now-required 'rules / lint' check until _schema is synced. Fix: have pin-consumers copy rules/core/_schema/ from the release tag into each consumer's rules/_schema/ on the same PR.
design: tools/pin_core.py apply takes --schema-dir (core rules/core/_schema at the release tag). It overwrites each rules/_schema/*.json in the consumer that also exists in core, matching RM015 (config.v1 is not vendored, so it is not added). Fails if the consumer has no matching file. Same all-or-nothing write as the pins. If the pin is already X.Y.Z but a schema differs, it syncs and reports changed=true. pin-consumers.yml checks out strspc-rules at inputs.tag into a separate path, because a dispatch of an older tag runs from main. No token or permission change: create-pull-request already commits everything under consumer/. Update the PR body, AGENTS.md, README.md and the release skill. Tests in tools/tests/test_pin_core.py.
acceptance_criteria: A core release's pin PR in each consumer also updates rules/_schema/ to the tag, and rules / lint passes on it with RM015 active.

PR #95 open against develop. Depends on strspc-manager-h80 for the manager leg of the next release.
CLI develop has WithDependencyFetcher (#153), #154 promotes it. RM015 is a Warning but the org lint runs --strict, so drift fails rules / lint. All four consumers match v1.11.0 for bootstrap, entity.v1 and realm.v1 today, so the CLI release alone breaks nothing; the next core release with a schema change would.

title: GH#114: external standards references and coverage
description: Realms, entities and rules reference versioned external standards (OWASP ASVS, ECSS, IAB TCF) for provenance and for proving coverage to an auditor. Today only free-text reference notes exist. Full proposal in SteerSpec/strspc-rules#114.

Rule: standards clause references like owasp.asvs:2.1.1, prefix validated against the entity or realm declaration. Only state I rules count as evidence; P shows as mapped, not enforced. An overriding rule does not take on the replaced rule's mapping. Coverage report over the effective rule set. Release order: rules, manager, CLI.
acceptance_criteria: Rules define standards at realm, entity and rule level and the coverage semantics. realm.v1 and entity.v1 accept the fields. The five open questions are decided and recorded on GH#114. Manager lint rejects undeclared clause prefixes. CLI preserves the fields and provides the coverage report. KWRD declares RFC 2119.
notes:
PLB confirmed both uses (provenance and audit coverage) and asked to file on 2026-10-31. Open: whether SteerSpec holds full clause lists (licensing), mapping on Published rules, hash coverage, relation values, rule field name. Statement of applicability is out of scope, likely follow-up.
Decisions recorded on GH#114 on 2026-11-01: mapping is a standard note, not a rule field; add, revise, withdraw in any state with no rule revision; no clause lists; relation is implements or derived_from, required. Realm declaration sits in the realm object. KWRD declaration moves to step 4.
Draft rules are in PR 125. Manager step, from the adversarial review: realm-lint owns NTE-015 (checkSubRealms holds parent and sub-realm); rulelint must skip rather than fail realm tiers; warn for manifest-less sources and for a sub-realm source without its parent; keep standard out of both relationNoteTypes maps; exclude standard notes from CacheKey; call inherit.Effective with nil states and filter afterwards; walk all tree entities, since Inheritance skips those without inherits; apply discards replaced notes, so keep a replaced list and walk each hop's Overrides recursively; evaluate relation per note; rulerefs flags mitre.cwe:CWE-787 style content as RF001 in rendered notes, so treat declared ids as non-realm qualifiers. Open wording point for STDREF-009 and 010: tie the Note to the implements Reference (same id and version with different relations in parent and child).
PR 125 rule numbers moved: coverage rule set STDREF-010, identity 011, covered 012, mapped 013, lapsed 014 and 015, override 016; note rules NTE-013 to NTE-019. The wording point above is closed: mapped and lapsed now tie the Note to its own implements Reference. Manager also needs an RD check for NTE-018: rule revision moved with the body unchanged. The bead's earlier note uses the old numbers.
Schema step: entity.v1 and realm.v1 need minItems 1 on standards and minLength 1 on version and url, because omitempty hides empty values from the structs and lint can't see them. Add a standard note to the manager's testdata/clean with the core pin. CLI step: its next-step hints omit --recursive, so RL029 is missed without it; strspc lint on single files never reaches RL029.
Correction to the CLI step note: RL031 (was RL029) now runs in realm validate with or without --recursive, so the CLI hints need no change for it. Standards codes moved to RL028 to RL031 after strspc-manager PR 223 took RL026 and RL027.

title: Make the override and inheritance rules ready to Publish (assessment 2026-11-25)
description: Assessment of dev.steerspec.core at e62fee9 (v1.25.0 plus #197) found the override model (RUL-018 to RUL-023, NTE-042 to NTE-044, ENT-011 to ENT-019) not ready to be Published. Children hold one finding each. The full report is in this issue's design field. Children labelled before-release change what strspc-manager-wcj builds and should be settled in Draft text before the next core release.
design:
# dev.steerspec.core assessment before the next release (2026-11-25)

Scope: develop at e62fee9, which is v1.25.0 (already tagged and on main) plus #197. The release in question is the one after 1.25.0.

Method: read all 251 rules and their Notes; scripted the citation and supersession graph; built a sandbox with an upstream realm, an organisation realm that inherits and overrides it, a grandchild Entity, a Standard Realm and a consumer project, and ran strspc 1.41.1 on it.

## Verdict

- The release can be cut. Everything #197 adds is Draft. Lint, realm validate and diff against v1.25.0 are clean, and CI and Build Schema passed on e62fee9.
- The override model (RUL-018 to RUL-023, NTE-042 to NTE-044, ENT-011 to ENT-019) is not ready to be Published.
- The release unblocks strspc-manager-wcj. Findings 1, 2 and 7 change what the manager builds, so settle them in Draft text first.

## Inheritance and overriding

### Settle before the release

1. **RUL-021 against consumer configuration.** A Published override of an Implemented rule is enforced as Implemented.
   - SPCFG-009 and SPCFGFAIL-002 filter on "rule lifecycle state codes". Nothing says they read the enforced state, so `evaluate_on: [I]` may drop both the override and its target.
   - SPCFG-008 says the consumer, not the rule, sets severity; with `fail_on: [I]` a Published rule now fails the run.
   - Published has no unenforced window for such an override, against the guidance of RULST-009/02. A stricter override has to stay Draft until the code complies.
   - A dependency bump in which upstream promotes the target to Implemented starts enforcing the child's Published override with no change in the child.
   - The first commit of #197 used the other design (an override applies once its state reaches the target's) and it was reworked after review. Under that design the same bump would silently bring the inherited rule back, so the merged design is the more stable one.
   - Remedy: Draft edits. State that `evaluate_on` and `fail_on` read the enforced state, and add a Note on the missing Published window.
2. **strspc-manager-wcj is stale.** Its title and description describe the dropped design ("once it reaches the target's state"). Rewrite it from RUL-018 to RUL-023 before anyone implements it.
7. **Coverage drops when an override is Published.** STDREF-010 removes the inherited rule, and STDREF-012 counts only state Implemented.
   - Sandbox, 1.41.1: an inherited Implemented rule covered clause 4.1. A Published override with its own `standard` Note turned it to "mapped"; without the Note it was "lapsed".
   - Under RUL-021 that override is enforced as Implemented, so the figure falls while enforcement does not.
   - Remedy: Draft edit to STDREF-012, or accept the drop and say so in a Note.

### Settle before these rules are Published

3. **"Effective rule set" is never defined.** ENT-009, RUL-009, RUL-018 and RUL-019 use it. Two readings exist for chains: the parent's set net of its own overrides, or not. The manager uses the netted reading (a grandchild inherited the parent's Published override, and RR015 rejected overriding the original target). Remedy: one new Draft rule defining the term, since ENT-009 and RUL-009 are Published.
4. **Two words for one thing.** RUL-009, RUL-018, RUL-020, RUL-021, NTE-042 and STDREF-015 say "replaces"; RUL-019 and STDREF-010 say "takes precedence over". Draft RUL-018 also contradicts the unconditional "replaces" of Published RUL-009. Remedy: Draft edits, and consider superseding RUL-009.
5. **Upstream changes to an overridden rule.** No core rule covers it.
   - Sandbox: when upstream published a successor, the child inherited the overridden rule and the unmodified successor together.
   - When upstream retired the target, the child held the successor and its own former override side by side. `strspc check` warned (RR016); `realm validate`, `lint` and `render` did not.
   - A Published override can't be retargeted (RUL-007). Superseding it with a rule that names the successor worked in the CLI, but RUL-011 only speaks of restating the same target.
   - The sandbox dependency was an unpinned local path, so this models the state after a bump, not the bump.
   - Remedy: new Draft rules for a dead override and for retargeting through supersession.
6. **Superseding an override.** RUL-019 keeps a Published or Implemented predecessor in precedence while its successor is Draft. What is missing is when the "lapses" of RUL-011 takes effect for a successor that drops `overrides`. Remedy: new Draft rule.
8. **Adopting a standard is unspecified.** The standards design names an "adopt" model (inheriting a standard's text as a project's own rules) as a non-goal, to come after #35.
   - Nothing forbids it today: the sandbox Entity inherited and overrode a Standard Realm Entity with no diagnostic.
   - Adopted rules are never Implemented (STDRLM-010) and never evaluated (STDRLM-011), so they enforce nothing.
   - An override of one gets no clause link: STDREF-016 maps it only by its own `standard` Notes, and Standard Realm rules carry `clause`, not Notes.
   - The path that exists for enforcing a standard is a Standard Reference with a `realm`, the organisation's own rules with `standard` Notes, and `exclusion` Notes.
9. **The upstream owner's controls are coarse and Draft.**
   - Visibility is per Entity and defaults to `public`, core's own Entities included. ENT-011 to ENT-019 are Draft while `inherits` and `overrides` are Published.
   - There is no per-Rule lock. ENT-015 and ENT-019 make a chain as narrow as its narrowest Entity, and inheritance is single, so one child can't derive from a baseline that mixes locked and tailorable rules.
   - A child of a `protected` Entity that omits `visibility` defaults to `public` and fails ENT-015 (RR024 in the sandbox).
11. **`override_ack` records an act, not an approval.** "A contributor of its Realm" adds nothing to CTRB-005, the author can acknowledge their own rule, and same-realm overrides need it too. A Draft edited after it was acknowledged needs a second Note, since NTE-044 freezes the first.

### Later

10. **No waiver.** Tailoring is add, extend (`extends` Note) or replace. An inherited rule can't be declared not applicable; the workaround is an override with a MAY body, which coverage reports as lapsed.
12. **Derivation is per Entity.** Parent sub-entities aren't inherited (ENT-006/01) and EUIDs can't collide with a dependency (RLM-006), so a 20-Entity baseline needs 20 child Entities. Chains stop at three hops (ENT-008).
13. **Retired.** RULST-010 says a Retired rule is still in force. Notes ENT-006/01 and ENT-019/01 say it is not, and ENT-009 doesn't inherit it. Revise the Notes.
14. **Tooling.** `realm validate --recursive --strict` reported nothing where `render` printed RR015, RR023 and RR024, and where `check` printed RR016. This is a strspc-manager issue.
15. **Identity providers.** CTRB-002/01 lists only `github`, and CTRB-002 and CTRB-003 are Implemented. An organisation on another provider can't author compliant rules. Goes with #135.

## Decisions

1. Keep "precedence from Published, enforced as Implemented" and close its gaps (findings 1 and 7)? Recommended: yes.
2. Adopting a Standard Realm Entity: forbid `inherits` until the adopt model is designed, or specify it now? Recommended: forbid for now.
3. Per-Rule lock, or visibility per Entity only? Recommended: per Entity for now, with an inheriting Entity defaulting to the inherited Entity's visibility.
4. A waiver for an inherited rule, or keep the MAY override? Recommended: keep the override for now.
5. `override_ack`: keep as a marker, or require a contributor other than the rule's author? Recommended: keep as a marker until #135.

## Rest of the rule set

- 251 rules: 131 Draft, 32 Published, 78 Implemented, 9 Retired, 1 Abandoned.
- STDREF (28), STDRLM (21) and STDCWK (7) are all Draft while CI coverage gates depend on STDREF (#185).
- NTE-007 to NTE-019 are Draft. NTE-005/01, on an Implemented rule, cites NTE-008 to NTE-011. RLMMNFST-004/01, on a Published rule, cites Draft RLM-015 and RLIFRMT-008.
- No Published or Implemented rule body cites a Draft, Abandoned or missing rule.
- RULST-011 is Abandoned, so no core rule lists the allowed transitions; RULST-012 stands alone.
- RUL-009/01 and RULST-008 predate RULST-012 (strspc-rules-aop).
- RL027 info on Draft RLMMNFST-006, RLMMNFST-008 and RLMMNFST-010.
- All 9 Retired rules have an Implemented successor.

## Not tested

- RUL-018 to RUL-023: strspc 1.41.1 predates #197 and applies a Draft override at once.
- `tools/build-schema.py --check` locally (`jsonschema` is missing); the Build Schema workflow passed on e62fee9.
- AI evaluation on the sandbox.
- A Standard Reference linked to a Standard Realm.
- The only real override in the org is GOTEST-002 in strspc-manager, same-realm and Draft. Cross-realm overrides are unexercised outside the sandbox.

design:
# Readiness of STDREF, STDRLM and STDCWK to be Published (2026-11-27)

Current state: the section "Batch 1 list" at the end is the one to act on. The sections before it are the record of how it was reached; where they differ (35 ready rules, the first STDRLM-013 proposal, 28 supporting rules), the later section wins.

Scope: develop at fcf055c (core 1.27.0). 56 rules, all Draft: STDREF 28, STDRLM 21, STDCWK 7, with 21 Notes.

Method: read every rule and Note; listed, group by group, the rules each group rests on, by cited ID and by term; compared with strspc-manager origin/main (3a97785) and strspc-CLI origin/main (1911bea); promoted STDREF-001, STDREF-010 and STDRLM-013 in a scratch worktree with strspc 1.44.0 and ran realm validate, lint, diff (all --strict), check --static-only and build-schema --check. The worktree was discarded; nothing in rules/core changed.

## Verdict

- 35 rules are ready, provided the Draft rules they rest on are Published with them.
- 10 rules, the ones that define covered, mapped, lapsed and the figures, are blocked by the override model (RUL-019, RUL-021, RUL-024, ENT-020), which strspc-rules-9sf holds as not ready.
- 3 rules wait on the adopt design (strspc-rules-9sf.7).
- 1 rule (STDRLM-013) needs a Draft fix, and then RULST-012 and STDRLM-010 Published with it.
- 7 rules (STDCWK) should be held: nothing implements them and one has a defect.
- No gate flag of GH#185 becomes fully backed by Published text until the 10 blocked rules are Published, because each flag depends on "covered" (STDREF-012).

## The decision that fixes the rest

Every one of the 56 rests on at least one Draft rule outside the three entities. The tools accept that: with STDREF-010 Published and RUL-019 Draft, validate, lint, diff, check --static-only and the schema check were all clean. It is a convention only, and so far core keeps it: no Published or Implemented rule body cites a Draft rule (assessment of 2026-11-25).

- Option A (recommended): keep the convention. Publish the Draft rules that the standards rules rest on in the same batch.
- Option B: allow Published text to rest on Draft text. Then the 10 blocked rules could go now, but their meaning could still move with RUL-019.

Decided by PLB on 2026-11-27: option A, as a principle. Within one Realm a Published Rule must not rest on a Draft Rule: it puts the cart before the horse and makes the Published text unstable. Building on a Draft Rule from outside, as tools and other Realms do, is what the Draft state is for. A core rule that states this is proposed in strspc-rules-sih (see that issue).

### Pass over the supporting rules (2026-11-27)

- The set closes at 28: beyond them, these rules rest only on Published or Implemented rules (RLM-010 to RLM-014, RLM-023, RUL-007, RSTHSH-001 and 002).
- NTE-017 to NTE-019 (retyping and withdrawing a `standard` Note) belong to the same feature and are Draft; publish them in the same batch, which then covers NTE-013 to NTE-019 of strspc-rules-0j2.
- NTE-026, NTE-027 and NTE-028 supersede Implemented NTE-021, NTE-022 and NTE-003. Once Published they stand beside their predecessors until they are Implemented and the predecessors Retired.
- RLMMNFST-010 says the licence MUST be an SPDX license identifier. Lint checks only that a Standard Realm has one. To decide before it is final: whether a `LicenseRef-` value is allowed for a standard whose licence is not on the SPDX list, since STDRLM-003 makes the field mandatory.
- All 28 except NTE-026 to NTE-028 are cited by ID in strspc-manager's Go code.
- No Published or Implemented rule body cites a Draft rule today (scripted check). Notes on such rules do, nine times: NTE-005/01 (NTE-008 to NTE-011), NTE-005/02 (NTE-008, NTE-029, RLMMNFST-014; added in #213) and RLMMNFST-004/01 (RLM-015, RLIFRMT-008).

Draft rules the 35 ready rules rest on (at least 28: this is the first hop, and these rules were not assessed one by one, nor traced for Draft rules of their own):

- ENT-017, RLMMNFST-007 to RLMMNFST-014: the `standards` array, `kind`, `license`, `attribution`, Realm Notes and the manifest hash.
- NTE-013 to NTE-016: `standard` Notes. These are also in strspc-rules-0j2.
- NTE-026 to NTE-035: Realm Notes and `exclusion` Notes.
- RUL-015 to RUL-017: `clause` and `profiles`.
- RLM-016, RLM-020: Realm tree.

Two of them carry lint info RL027 (possibly two statements, RUL-004): RLMMNFST-008, on which STDRLM-001 rests, and RLMMNFST-010. Publishing freezes them, so each is split or confirmed as one statement first (the same question as strspc-rules-bfm).

## Ready, with the rules above (35)

- STDREF-001 to STDREF-009: the reference itself and inheritance.
- STDREF-011: clause identity. See open point 1 of GH#185 below.
- STDREF-017 to STDREF-022, STDREF-027: linked Standard Realm, profile, clause list, exclusion.
- STDRLM-001 to STDRLM-009, STDRLM-012, STDRLM-014 to STDRLM-018: manifest fields, clause list, profiles, supersession.
- STDRLM-019 to STDRLM-021: verbatim bodies. See finding 5.

All STDREF rules and STDRLM-002 to 006, 008 to 018 are cited in strspc-manager's Go code. STDRLM-001, 007, 019, 020 and 021 are not cited by ID, but lint does skip RL021 and RL026 in a Standard Realm, which is what 020 and 021 allow.

## Blocked by the override model (10)

STDREF-010, 012 and 015 name "replaces under RUL-019" or the enforced state of RUL-024 and RUL-021. The others use a term those three define:

- STDREF-013 (coverage rule set), STDREF-014 (neither covered nor mapped)
- STDREF-023 (unmapped), STDREF-024, 025, 026 and 028 (the figures)

strspc-rules-9sf.6 records that RUL-019 r1 implies, without deciding it, that the inherited Rule returns when an override is Retired. That decision can change what STDREF-010 and 015 mean, so these wait for 9sf.5 and 9sf.6.

## Waiting on the adopt design (3)

PLB decided on 2026-11-25 (9sf.7) to specify the adopt model, and listed as open: how adopted rules are evaluated given STDRLM-010 and STDRLM-011, and the clause link of a rule that overrides an adopted rule (STDREF-016). Publishing these three first would fix the text the design is meant to settle.

## Fix in Draft first (1): STDRLM-013

STDRLM-013 says the superseded Rule MUST enter Terminated when its successor enters Published. That holds only for a Published predecessor:

- Published predecessor: permitted only by RULST-012 (Draft, r2); RULST-011 is Abandoned. RULST-012 has to be Published with it.
- Draft predecessor: STDRLM-017 allows it, since a Draft Rule that supersedes nothing is live (STDRLM-014). No core rule lets a Draft Rule enter Terminated; its terminal state is Abandoned (RULST-004). The rule can't be met.
- Implemented predecessor: excluded only by STDRLM-010, which is held. Implemented to Terminated skips Retired.

Proposed text (to confirm): "When a Rule of a Standard Realm that supersedes a Published Rule enters Published, the superseded Rule MUST enter Terminated in the same change." The Draft-predecessor case then needs its own answer: forbid it in STDRLM-017, or say the predecessor is Abandoned. strspc-rules-aop (wording of RULST-008 and RUL-009/01) is related and does not block.

## Hold (7): STDCWK-001 to STDCWK-007

- Not implemented: no Go code in strspc-manager cites them, strspc-CLI's docs/standards.md says "crosswalk between editions is not yet implemented", and core has no schema for the file.
- Not exercised: the pilot repository strspc-std-owasp-asvs is empty.
- Defect in STDCWK-002: the file is `_crosswalk/<edition>.json`, and an edition is a free string. `ISO 27001:2022` (the example of STDREF-007/03) holds a space and a colon, which is not a valid file name on Windows; an edition with a slash breaks the path.
- Gap in STDCWK-005: no kind sets how many clauses `to` holds, so `moved` with three targets is valid.
- No gate depends on them.

## Findings on wording

1. STDREF-016 says a Rule "IS mapped". STDREF-013 makes mapped a property of a clause. To reword with the adopt design.
2. STDREF-014 and STDREF-015 say "an Entity it inherits from". STDREF-010 says "acquires under ENT-009", which covers the whole chain. State whether a grandparent counts. Both are in the blocked group, so there is time.
3. STDREF-014 counts a clause as lapsed when its Rule is Retired. RULST-010 says a Retired Rule is still in force. To confirm as intended (related: 9sf.11).
4. STDREF-022: a reference declared in an Entity file can carry `realm` (the schema allows it) but can never have exclusions, since an exclusion is a Realm Note of the declaring manifest (NTE-034). strspc-manager does this on purpose ("a reference an entity declares excludes nothing"). A clarification Note would say so; it can be added after publication.
5. STDRLM-021 is an exception to NTE-020, which is Implemented and has no "except". Add a clarification Note on NTE-020 that points to it. STDRLM-020 permits what no core rule forbids: only lint RL021 asks for a Key Word.

## The two open points of GH#185

- STDREF-011 and crosswalks: final as it stands. A crosswalk maps the clauses of one edition to those of another, so it presumes they are distinct, which is what STDREF-011 says. One residual case: `version` is optional (STDREF-007), so adding a version to a reference later re-identifies all its clauses and a saved baseline reports them as changed. A Note can say so.
- STDREF-022 and `--allow-excluded`: no conflict. The rule defines the status. An exclusion removes a clause from the divisor (STDREF-024) and so raises the figure; the CLI asking the caller to allow a new exclusion fits the intent of NTE-033.

## Proposed order

1. Decide option A or B.
2. Batch 1: the supporting rules (36 after the second pass below, plus two from the split, less any held) with the 35 ready rules. Covers strspc-rules-0j2 for NTE-007 to NTE-011 and NTE-013 to NTE-019.
3. Decide 9sf.5 and 9sf.6, then batch 2: the override rules (ENT-020 included) with the 10 coverage rules. This is the batch GH#185 needs.
4. Adopt design (9sf.7), then STDRLM-010, STDRLM-011 and STDREF-016. STDRLM-013 goes with this batch, after its Draft fix, together with RULST-012 once that rule is assessed.
5. STDCWK after the pilot has a crosswalk.

## Not tested

- A sandbox with a linked Standard Realm on strspc 1.44.0. The behaviour above is read from strspc-manager's code and comments.
- The supporting rules, rule by rule, and RULST-012.
- Whether `strspc diff` rejects a Draft or an Implemented Rule entering Terminated; the STDRLM-013 finding is read from the rules.
- Citation in strspc-manager is by rule ID in Go code; a rule not cited may still be enforced.

## Assessment of the supporting rules (2026-11-27, second pass)

Decided by PLB the same day: split the two-part rules RLMMNFST-008 and RLMMNFST-010; allow a custom licence value.

Method: read the 31 rules and their Notes (the 28 above and NTE-017 to NTE-019); built a sandbox on strspc 1.44.0 with a Standard Realm (three clauses, two profiles, a `LicenseRef-` licence) and a project realm that depends on it, links it, maps two rules, excludes a clause and adds Realm Notes; broke each thing in turn and ran realm validate --strict and standards coverage. The linked Standard Realm that the 2026-11-25 assessment left untested is now exercised.

### Verdict

Of the 31: 26 are ready as they stand; 2 need the split (RLMMNFST-008, RLMMNFST-010); 2 hang on the hash decision (RLMMNFST-013, RLMMNFST-014); 1 may be held with the adopt design (RUL-017, finding 9). Five more rules belong in the batch (NTE-007 to NTE-011). They were read, not sandboxed, and NTE-010 was reworded on 2026-11-27 (#213).

### What the sandbox confirmed (tool matches the text)

- `kind` other than `standard` fails the schema; a rule with `clause` or `profiles` is refused outside a Standard Realm.
- A Standard Realm without licence, edition or attribution is reported.
- A `standard` Note without `<id>:<clause>`, with a blank clause or duplicated on its rule is refused; an undeclared id and a clause outside the linked list are reported by validate.
- A clause above the claimed profile may be mapped and stays out of the figure.
- Retyping a `standard` Note to `reference` on an Implemented rule works, leaves the rule's revision at 0, raises the Note's revision and drops the clause from coverage.
- Realm Notes: an exclusion needs a ref naming a linked reference of its manifest; a ref is refused on other types; numbering gaps and a wrong type are reported; an exclusion is withdrawn only by retyping to `reference`, and can't be turned back.
- Coverage: 1 of 2 covered (50 %) before the exclusion, 1 of 1 (100 %) after it.
- The manifest hash is recomputed by every CLI write once present, and a hand edit is reported.

### Findings

1. RLMMNFST-013 says a manifest HAS a hash, an absolute requirement. The tools keep it optional: `realm init` writes none and a manifest without one is not reported. No realm in the org carries one: core and all seven consumers have none. To decide before it is final: required (then core and the consumers add it with `strspc realm rehash`, the release bump and the pin PRs recompute it, and lint reports a missing one), or optional (reword in Draft). RLMMNFST-014 follows the same answer.
2. RLMMNFST-010: the tools check only that a Standard Realm has a licence, not its form; `All rights reserved` passes. Allowing `LicenseRef-` values matches what the tool accepts today; checking the form is a strspc-manager follow-up.
3. NTE-034: an exclusion may name a clause that is not in the linked clause list (sandbox: `9.9` accepted by `realm note add` and by validate). It doesn't change the figure. A `standard` Note has that check (STDREF-021); an exclusion has no rule for it. Additive: a new Draft rule can follow.
4. NTE-017 to NTE-019 and the Realm Note rules use the Note revision, no-removal and sequential-identifier rules (NTE-008, NTE-009, NTE-011), which are Draft. NTE-007 and NTE-010 are the remaining two of that group and rest on nothing Draft outside the batch. All five join batch 1. NTE-012 stays Draft: it rests on the visibility rules of strspc-rules-9sf.
5. NTE-026, NTE-027 and NTE-028 supersede Implemented NTE-021, NTE-022 and NTE-003. Once Published they stand beside their predecessors until they are Implemented and the predecessors Retired.
6. RLMMNFST-012/01 (a Note) cites Draft RLM-022, a language rule outside the batch. RULST-013 covers bodies only, so it doesn't block.
7. RLMMNFST-006 has the same two-part form (lint RL027) and is outside the batch, with the other language rules.
8. Outside the 31: `strspc rule promote` lets a rule of a Standard Realm enter Implemented; only lint reports it afterwards (STDRLM-010).

9. RUL-017 keeps `clause` and `profiles` out of code Realms. The adopt design (strspc-rules-9sf.7) lists the clause link of a rule that overrides an adopted rule as open, and may want that link in a code Realm. Nothing in batch 1 rests on RUL-017, so holding it with the adopt group costs nothing. The licence and attribution rules can go: a carry-over rule for adoption would be additive.
10. STDRLM-013 and STDRLM-017 (first pass, "Fix in Draft first"): the simplest fix is in STDRLM-017, which is in the ready group, so it has to be settled before batch 1. Proposed STDRLM-017 r1: "A Rule of a Standard Realm MUST supersede only a Published Rule." A Draft rule is edited in place and needs no successor, and an Implemented one can't exist there. STDRLM-013 then holds as written and can join batch 1 with RULST-012, the rule that permits Published to Terminated.
11. Recommendation on finding 1: required. The tool's own text for RM025 says the hash stays optional "until the CLI recomputes it on every write", and that work is done (strspc-CLI#284).

Limits of the sandbox: the withdrawal checks retyped a Note without trying to change its content in the same step, so "content unchanged" on withdrawal (NTE-019, NTE-035) is untested.

### Proposed split (texts to approve)

- RLMMNFST-008 r1: "MAY declare a `kind` field in the `realm` object."
- New RLMMNFST-015: "The value of `kind` MUST be `standard`."
- RLMMNFST-010 r1: "MAY declare a `license` field in the `realm` object."
- New RLMMNFST-016: "The value of `license` MUST be an SPDX license identifier or match `^LicenseRef-[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$`." The pattern is the SPDX form for a licence that is not on its list.
- Notes on RLMMNFST-016: rationale (many standards carry terms that are not on the SPDX License List, and `LicenseRef-` is the form SPDX gives for such a licence) and example (`CC-BY-SA-4.0`, `LicenseRef-ECSS-Terms`).
- `realm.v1.schema.json` is maintained by hand; its descriptions of `kind` and `license` cite RLMMNFST-008 and RLMMNFST-010 and say "SPDX license identifier". Updating them needs PLB's approval.

### Not tested

- Sub-realms: a Realm Note or a linked reference in a sub-realm, and resolution of a `standard` Note through a Realm's parent.
- A reference declared in an Entity file.
- `strspc diff` on the Note rules (removal, renumbering); known from earlier PRs (RD012, RD013, RD015, RD016).

## Batch 1 list (2026-11-27, prepared for PLB's approval; nothing promoted)

After #218 (RULST-013) and #219 (splits, LicenseRef, STDRLM-017 r1). develop at 349b1e9. 74 rules, all Draft, to promote to Published with `strspc rule promote`.

Standards rules (36):
- STDREF-001 to 009, 011, 017 to 022, 027 (17)
- STDRLM-001 to 009, 012, 013, 014 to 021 (19)

Supporting rules (38):
- RULST-012: a Published Rule may go to Terminated once its successor is Published (STDRLM-013 rests on it)
- ENT-017, RLMMNFST-007 to 016 (11): the `standards` arrays, `kind`, `license`, `attribution`, Realm Notes, manifest hash
- NTE-007 to 011 (5): Note references, revision, no removal, frozen types, sequential identifiers
- NTE-013 to 019 (7): `standard` Notes
- NTE-026 to 035 (10): Notes on a Rule or a Realm, Realm Notes, exclusions
- RUL-015, RUL-016 (2): `clause`, `profiles`
- RLM-016, RLM-020 (2): Realm tree

Held, not in the batch: STDREF-010, 012 to 016, 023 to 026, 028 (override model and adopt design); STDRLM-010, STDRLM-011 (adopt design); RUL-017 (adopt design); STDCWK-001 to 007; NTE-012 (visibility); the language rules RLM-017 to 019, 021, 022, RLMMNFST-006 and 017 (not assessed).

Checks run on the list:
- Every rule ID cited in a body of the batch is Published, Implemented or in the batch (scripted). RULST-013 holds.
- Trial in a scratch worktree with strspc 1.44.0: all 74 promotions succeed (NTE-026 to 028, which supersede Implemented rules, included); realm validate, lint and diff with --strict, check --static-only, build-schema --check and the 70 tool tests are clean. Result: 106 Published, 78 Implemented, 70 Draft, 9 Retired, 1 Abandoned. The worktree was discarded.
- Notes on batch rules that cite a Draft rule outside it (allowed, bodies only): NTE-010/01 (NTE-044), RLMMNFST-012/01 (RLM-022).

To carry in the batch PR: docs/rules.md lines that say the standards rules and RULST-012 are Draft.

Written or reworded on 2026-11-27, and so final within a day of their text: RLMMNFST-008 r1, RLMMNFST-010 r1, RLMMNFST-015, RLMMNFST-016, STDRLM-017 r1, NTE-010 r1.

title: GH#207: add refs.coverage to config.v1 for rule-citation coverage
description:

Prompts, agent instructions and docs list rule IDs by hand and nothing fails when a rule is added; the fix is a coverage check declared in .strspc/config.yaml. title: GH#42: rule scoping, map rules to code paths and patterns
description: SteerSpec/strspc-rules#42 (opened 2026-03-26, no bead until the 2026-11-27 cross-check). Rules have no structured way to say which parts of a codebase they apply to, so every rule is evaluated against everything. The issue proposes an entity-level scope field (paths, languages, imports) with a config.yaml override, and lists open questions (optional or mandatory, negation, sub-realms). Not delivered as of core 1.26.0: the entity schema has no scope field. Related pieces that exist: the Note type applies_to is in the schema enum and the CLI (strspc note add --type applies_to --body 'src/cmd/*.go'), but no core rule defines what it means; refs.coverage (SPCFGCOV, #208) maps Entities to files for citations, not for evaluation. First step is a design decision: build on applies_to Notes, add an entity scope field, or both. Downstream: strspc-manager ruleresolve and ruleeval, strspc-CLI config and check.
acceptance_criteria: A design is agreed with PLB and written as core rules (Draft), or the issue is closed as superseded with the reason recorded.
